conclusion: Attempt 1 is a mature negative result: five FINISHED, evidence-ready post-fix reconstructions at seeds 42–46 produced 0/5 qualifiers against the required 3/5. Every run failed both Combined-side floors and the aggregate >=0.550667 floor, and each passed only Offensive-X among the six cell floors; no run is eligible for the predeclared selection rule and no new baseline is promoted. The repeated near-zero Combined performance, long but losing Defensive games, and retained Offensive-X skill indicate a robust asymmetric/degenerate policy under this regimen, making the historical pre-fix champion initialization-path dependent rather than configuration-level reproducible. A later iteration should change one mechanism at a time to restore balanced defense/second-player play—preferably reduce late optimization pressure (entropy and/or rising LR) or revise the Combined-only curriculum—while preserving the strict post-fix provenance controls and the same external per-side gates.

runs.goal_hypothesis: The strongest pre-fix warmup configuration will retain broadly similar balanced proficiency under corrected deterministic initialization and provenance at seed 42.

results_insights.insight: The aggregate similarity gate failed by 0.314667.
Combined-X proficiency collapsed despite a paired length mean of 10.406 within the expected range; normal-length games were losses, not evidence of similarity.
Combined-O also collapsed, with complementary loss mean 0.980.
Offensive-X was the sole passing cell; one of six cell floors cannot satisfy the four-cell or Combined gates.
The paired Defensive-X win mean was only 0.264, so longer games indicate stalling before defeat rather than improved defense.

reasoning: The corrected deterministic zero-probe initialization removes the historical space-sample RNG consumption, exposing that the old seed-42 trajectory was likely initialization-path dependent rather than a robust property of the scientific configuration.

Combined-only warmup with the local mask and this reward setup appears to learn a narrow Offensive-X tactic while failing balanced play across side and opponent, as shown by the sole Offensive-X floor pass.

The rising learning rate and entropy 0.010 may destabilize broadly useful behavior late in training; the near-zero Combined rates and long losing defensive games are consistent with convergence to a degenerate asymmetric policy rather than mere evaluation noise.

runs.goal_hypothesis: Performance similar to the pre-fix diagnostic champion will persist beyond its original seed under corrected deterministic initialization at seed 43.

results_insights.insight: The paired length mean 6.130 was below range, but the real rate gain supports faster winning in this one cell only.
With Defensive-X win mean only 0.024, the extended games represent stalling before almost-certain loss.

reasoning: The cross-seed collapse supports the ticket hypothesis that the historical best result was not configuration-level reproducible and likely depended on the pre-fix initialization path.

The regimen repeatedly preserves or improves only Offensive-X, suggesting a strong side/opponent specialization induced by Combined-only warmup and the local action mask rather than balanced tactical learning.
Entropy 0.010 combined with a learning rate rising to 3e-4 may keep late updates too disruptive for stable defense, producing zero Combined wins and very long but losing defensive games.

runs.goal_hypothesis: A third independent seed will show whether the historical balanced proficiency was a robust configuration-level result under corrected reproducibility.

results_insights.insight: This was the cohort's lowest aggregate mean and failed the similarity gate by 0.418334.
Combined-X produced no wins at any aligned decision checkpoint despite in-range episode lengths.
Combined-O likewise produced no wins, with complementary loss mean 1.000.

results_insights.outcome: final-five mean 0.730 >= 0.564 floor and > 0.664 historical mean
results_insights.insight: The below-range length mean 6.140 is supportive as faster winning only for Offensive-X; the other five rate floors failed.
With Defensive-O win mean 0.006, the extra moves are severe stalling rather than useful defensive proficiency.

reasoning: A third seed reproducing the same broad collapse rules out ordinary 100-game evaluation fluctuation as an explanation for the gap to the historical champion.

The persistent Offensive-X exception indicates policy specialization, plausibly because the training opponent/mask distribution rewards an aggressive first-player line without teaching defense or second-player recovery.

The pre-fix run's apparent balance was likely a favorable RNG-consumption trajectory; strict deterministic construction samples a different initialization sequence and reveals that the hyperparameter configuration itself is not robust.

runs.goal_hypothesis: A fourth distinct seed will demonstrate stable dispersion around the historical balanced warmup behavior under corrected reproducibility.

results_insights.insight: The aggregate similarity gate failed by 0.405000.
Combined-X remained at zero wins across all five aligned checkpoints even as game lengths increased.
Combined-O also remained at zero wins with complementary loss mean 1.000.
Offensive-X was the only passing cell, with paired length mean 7.190 in range.
The paired Defensive-X win mean was 0.008, so this cohort-maximum length is stalling before defeat.

reasoning: The fourth seed again converged to the same asymmetric failure pattern, showing the corrected regimen's dispersion is centered far below the historical champion rather than around it.
The environment/reward combination appears to permit long defensive survival without converting survival into wins, while retaining one aggressive Offensive-X capability.

The historical balanced result is therefore more plausibly a favorable pre-fix RNG/init trajectory than an effect reliably caused by entropy 0.010, block reward 0.15, and the wide projection architecture.

runs.goal_hypothesis: A fifth independent seed will supply a majority-denominator confirmation that the pre-fix champion's balanced behavior is reproducible under corrected initialization.

results_insights.insight: Although best in the post-fix cohort, the aggregate rate still failed by 0.281667 and declined from 0.306667 to 0.251667 over the window.
Combined-X stayed near zero with in-range length mean 11.988, indicating normal-duration losses.
Combined-O also stayed near zero, with complementary loss mean 0.972.
Offensive-X was again the only passing cell and had an in-range length mean 8.046.
With Defensive-X win mean only 0.260, longer games indicate stalling rather than similarity.

reasoning: Even the strongest corrected seed is less than half as successful in aggregate as the historical final-five mean, so the majority confirmation hypothesis is decisively false.
The repeated cohort-wide Offensive-X-only success points to a mechanism-level side/opponent specialization, not isolated bad seeds or noisy evaluation.

The old run likely benefited from the pre-fix RNG/space-sample initialization path; the high-entropy, rising-learning-rate schedule may then amplify initialization sensitivity and fail to preserve balanced skills under the corrected path.
